A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLPA study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated sections and appendix renumbering can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original ALOE benchmark experiments, reward ablations, preference-conflict and long-dialogue tests, and human evaluations of user and reward models.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental and human-evaluation results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The Qwen-based RLPA method, simulated-user interaction, profile and response rewards, and PPO optimization remain unchanged. Equation 4 relabels the response reward without changing its computation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ALOE training data, Vanilla ALOE evaluation, PersonaChat-derived Extended ALOE evaluation, and auxiliary user/reward-model evaluation datasets. Preference-conflict and long-dialogue scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the benchmark, reasoning-model, simulator, and reward-model comparisons. The two newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Training settings, evaluation samples, metrics, turn counts, and human-evaluation procedures are retained. The metrics discussion is rewritten in v2 Appendix C.3, but preserves the GPT-4o judging procedure and AL, N-IR, and N-R2 calculations.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same reward ablations, turn-6 preference shift, 70-turn profile-tracking test, reasoning-efficiency comparison, evaluator checks, and reward curves. Renumbered appendices do not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: The plotted bands and agreement statistics are unchanged, with no new run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions, or significance tests. The added checklist asserts statistical-significance reporting in Appendix F but supplies no additional statistical evidence.

E6.justification: Reported numerical and qualitative results are retained throughout the tables and figures. For example, Table 1 gives RLPA average alignment scores of 73.38 on Vanilla ALOE and 52.74 on Extended ALOE in both versions.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, reward definitions, PPO objective, and metric mathematics are unchanged. Equation 1 fixes the placement of summation limits, and Equation 4 clarifies notation; neither introduces new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about dynamic profile modeling, dual-reward interactive training, personalization performance, preference adaptation, and reasoning efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations and applicability boundaries remain unchanged. The single-user limitation and unresolved theoretical questions move from v1 Appendix A to v2 Section 8; the broader-impact discussion is also retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-repository address in the abstract and a checklist statement that code and data accompany supplementary files. Existing prompts, hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify the external resources.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zheng et al. (2024), Ali-Agent, in Section 3.1 and Qiu et al. (2025), Measuring What Makes You Unique, in Section 6. These are limited citation additions without substantive changes to research positioning.

P1.justification: The research narrative remains largely intact. v2 rephrases the metrics discussion, moves limitations into the main text, adds acknowledgments and a conference checklist, and updates author and conference information. Some checklist references retain outdated appendix labels.

P2.justification: The same 18 figures and 10 tables are retained, with changes to float placement, spacing, and small caption or label details. Table 1 standardizes the N-R2 heading, and Equation 1 receives corrected summation typesetting.

improvement.justification: The code-access pointer and notation corrections provide modest benefits, while the scientific evidence remains unchanged. However, the new checklist introduces reporting inconsistencies: it directs readers to Appendix F for human-subjects review information absent there and declares writing-only LLM use despite the LLM-based method. These access and clarity gains coexist with reduced reporting reliability, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
